plannedCharts.title: The Gulf's shipping lane emptied in a fortnight
plannedCharts.subtitle: Cargo carried through the Strait of Hormuz, seven-day moving average · IMF PortWatch via World Bank
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Everything in this article starts here. One sea lane carries most of the Gulf's oil and gas, and at the end of February 2026 it effectively stopped.

plannedCharts.title: Four prices that all run through one strait
plannedCharts.subtitle: Daily prices indexed to 27 February 2026, the last market day before the conflict · World Bank
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Oil is the headline, but the same strait carries the gas that heats Europe and the urea that feeds Indian wheat. Watching them together shows the shock was never only about petrol.

plannedCharts.title: South Asia is the region most exposed to Gulf energy
plannedCharts.subtitle: Share of economies in each region sourcing over 30% of their oil imports from the Middle East, 2023 · World Bank
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Before asking what the shock did to India, establish that India sits in the most exposed neighbourhood on earth.

plannedCharts.title: India could replace the barrel. It could not replace the cooking gas.
plannedCharts.unit: % of import value from the Gulf
plannedCharts.subtitle: Share of India's 2025 import value sourced from the seven Gulf economies · UN Comtrade
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: This single chart explains why the shock hit India so unevenly. The exposure is not one number, it is a gradient, and the top and bottom of it behaved completely differently.

plannedCharts.title: Where India's crude actually comes from
plannedCharts.subtitle: Share of India's 2025 crude oil import value, by supplier · UN Comtrade
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The reason crude volumes held: India spent the years after 2022 rebuilding its supplier list around a country that does not ship through Hormuz.

plannedCharts.title: Where India's cooking gas comes from
plannedCharts.subtitle: Share of India's 2025 LPG import value, by supplier · UN Comtrade
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The same chart for LPG, and the contrast with crude is the whole argument.

plannedCharts.title: What India actually paid for a barrel
plannedCharts.subtitle: Monthly average, India's realised crude import price against the reference benchmarks · PPAC and World Bank
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: There are two Indian oil prices and the difference matters enormously during a shock. One is a reference quote; the other is the money that actually left the country.

plannedCharts.title: The same barrels, a $22.8 billion bigger bill
plannedCharts.subtitle: Spending on crude oil imports, April to July of each year · PPAC
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: This is the cleanest measure of what the shock cost, because the volume barely moved. Almost the entire difference is price.

plannedCharts.title: Cooking gas was the thing India could not buy
plannedCharts.subtitle: LPG imports, April to July of each year · PPAC
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Crude was a price problem. LPG was a quantity problem, and quantity problems reach kitchens.

plannedCharts.title: The shock barely reached the shelf
plannedCharts.subtitle: Year-on-year consumer price inflation, July 2026 · MOSPI 2024-base CPI
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: If a landed crude price rises 81%, you would expect the pump to follow. It did not, and where that gap went is the rest of the story.

plannedCharts.title: It went to the exchequer instead
plannedCharts.subtitle: Change in central government revenue and subsidy lines, April-June 2026 against a year earlier · Comptroller General of Accounts
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The money that did not come out of household budgets came out of the government's. This is where to look for it.

plannedCharts.title: The World Bank cut 93 of 146 forecasts. India's went up.
plannedCharts.subtitle: How 2026 growth forecasts moved between the January and June 2026 Global Economic Prospects
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The oddity that makes this story worth telling: the edition that downgraded two-thirds of the developing world nudged India upward.

plannedCharts.title: Same number, completely different reasons
plannedCharts.subtitle: World Bank forecast for India's real GDP growth, by fiscal year · June 2026 edition
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: India's 2026-27 forecast moved by a tenth of a point between January and June. Everything behind it was replaced.

plannedCharts.title: India went into the shock accelerating
plannedCharts.subtitle: Real GDP growth, year on year, by calendar quarter · World Bank
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Part of why the shock did less damage than it might have is simply when it arrived. India hit it with momentum.

selectionRules: Start from the page question, not from the indicator name.
Choose the smallest set of visuals that explains scale, trend, structure, comparison, and caveat.
Prefer mobile-friendly charts: line charts with sparse ticks, horizontal bars, share strips, pyramids only when essential, and no dense tables.
Use one strong pull quote only when the evidence supports it with a number.
Add glossary blocks for technical terms that normal readers may not know.
caveats: Use only figures present in lockedNumbers or sourceSummaries.
If a related theme indicator is present, you may use it for context, but do not pretend it is the main answer.
If source coverage is thin, say so directly.
Do not compare states, districts, or cities unless the evidence packet contains those geographies.
forbiddenClaims: Do not infer causality from a trend unless the evidence explicitly supports it.
Do not cite a source that is not present in sourceSummaries.
